title: Sherpa Tensing — Descent Eight: Past Continuous Passive (B2)
description: The background of a story, with the doer taken out of it. Something was in the middle of happening to a thing when something else cut across — and who was…

hero.lede: The background of a story, with the doer taken out of it. Something was in the middle of happening to a thing when something else cut across — and who was doing it is either unknown or beside the point.

sections.label: Descent briefing
sections.title: When to use it
sections.lead: The passive is not a different tense. It is the past continuous with the doer let go — and the reason you let them go is always one of these six.

cards.head: You do not know who
cards.body: Nobody can tell you the doer, so the sentence does without one.

cards.head: The doer does not matter
cards.body: The event is the news; who did it is a footnote.
cards.ex: "The road was being resurfaced at the time."

cards.head: The doer is obvious
cards.body: Saying it would be a waste of everyone's time.
cards.ex: "He was being questioned when the lawyer arrived."

cards.head: You would rather not say
cards.body: The passive is how English removes a person from a sentence.

cards.head: Putting the important thing first
cards.body: Whatever you put at the front is what the sentence is about.

cards.head: Putting the doer back with by
cards.body: When the doer is the point, it goes at the end.
cards.ex: "The house was being painted by a firm from the village."

cards.head: Negative
cards.body: the not goes after the first auxiliary

cards.head: Questions
cards.body: the first auxiliary moves to the front

cards.head: With the doer
cards.ex: "It was being handled by the night shift."

charts.head: Turning an active sentence around
charts.note: Three moves, always the same: the object comes to the front, the verb becomes was / were + being + participle, and the old subject either disappears or goes to the back behind by. Only the middle step changes from camp to camp.

head: Active
Passive
What moved
rows: A firm was painting the house.
The house was being painted by a firm.
The firm stayed, at the end.

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Being never changes. Only was and were move, exactly as at camp six: was for I, he, she and it; were for the rest.

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this one is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: Without being, the road is doing the work itself.
Been belongs to the perfect. The continuous takes being.
The office was being watched for years.
The office had been watched for years.
A duration measured back needs a perfect, not the continuous.

charts.note: Neither is better. The question is only what the sentence is about — because whatever you put at the front is what the reader will think it is about.

head: Question
Passive
Active
rows:
The thing it happens to.
"The road was being resurfaced."

The one who does it.
"They were resurfacing the road."
Often not — and you do not need to.
Yes, and you are naming them.
At the end with by, or nowhere at all.
At the front, as the subject.
Longer by two or three words.
Usually shorter. Prefer it when both work.

charts.example: This is how a witness describes a scene they were not part of: the door was being forced, papers were being burned. It gives you the action in progress and admits you could not see who was doing it — which is often the honest sentence, not the evasive one.

sections.label: Trail markers
sections.title: Signal words

signals.head: Verbs with no passive at all

sections.example: The test for whether a verb can go passive: does it take an object? They built it has one, so it turns. It happened has none, so it cannot.

sections.title: The event, and the doer you dropped

diagram.intro: The block is the same block as the ascent, lit from above instead of fading into the dark — because the tense has not changed, only the light. Inside it sits a dashed box: the doer. It is drawn inside the event rather than beside it because the doer is not a moment in time, it is a part of the sentence — and it is dashed because most of the time nobody says it. Click either to see it in a sentence.

panels.head: The doer — optional, and usually gone
items: … without us, and by nobody we could name.

quiz.explain: Was + being + participle. Was watching would make the office the watcher.
Was being resurfaced puts the work in progress at that past moment.
Wards is plural, so were being, and rebuild / rebuilt / rebuilt.

quiz.prompt: The files _____ at that point. (not / copy)
quiz.explain: The not goes after were, then being, then the participle.
Was + subject + being + participle. Room is singular.
The questioning was already running when the lawyer cut across it.

quiz.prompt: The house _____ by a firm from the village. (paint)
quiz.explain: Was being painted, with the doer behind by.

quiz.hint: A finished event with a date.
quiz.explain: A date and a completed event take the past simple passive, not the continuous.
Was being followed says it was happening to me at the time.
Were being made — and notice how thoroughly the deciders vanish.

quiz.prompt: The papers _____ when the police came in. (burn)
quiz.explain: Papers is plural. Were burning would say the papers caught fire on their own.

quiz.prompt: We _____ to a different floor all that week. (move)
quiz.explain: Were being moved says it was happening to us.

quiz.prompt: The door _____ when I got there. (force)
quiz.explain: Was being forced puts it mid-action; was forced would report it finished.

quiz.prompt: The office _____ for years before anyone noticed. (watch)
quiz.explain: For years measured back from a past moment needs the past perfect, not the continuous.

results: Clean run. You can turn a sentence around and you know when the doer is worth keeping.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at the active version before you go on.
Good first attempt. The auxiliary chain is the part to read again.
